messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and for a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a thorough cleaning (strings, fretboard, body). Use the `tune_instrument` function if you’re unsure how to tune it to standard pitch. | A well‑maintained instrument looks more appealing and shows buyers you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture the whole body, headstock, strings, fretboard, and any imperfections. Use natural light and a neutral background. | Good photos attract more views and reduce the chance of buyer questions. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, and local classifieds. Look at similar models, ages, and conditions. | Knowing the going rate helps you price competitively. | | **4. Write a Clear Listing** | Include:
• Brand & model
• Age (or year)
• Condition (new, like new, used, etc.)
• Any upgrades or repairs
• Reason for selling
• Price | Transparency builds trust and reduces back‑and‑forth. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform** | • **Reverb** – great for musical instruments, global reach.
• **eBay** – auction or fixed price, large audience.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local Music Stores** – consignment or direct sale. | Pick the one that best matches your urgency, price, and shipping willingness. | | **6. Set a Realistic Price** | Start slightly above your target to allow room for negotiation. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a higher starting point keeps you from underselling. | | **7. Offer Shipping Options (if online)** | Provide a shipping estimate and use a reputable carrier. Offer “ship only” or “pick‑up only” options. | Clear shipping terms prevent confusion and protect both parties. | | **8. Screen Potential Buyers** | Ask about their experience level, why they want the guitar, and confirm they’re serious. | Reduces time wasted on non‑serious inquiries. | | **9. Meet Safely (for local sales)** | Arrange a public place (coffee shop, library, police station) and bring a friend if possible. | Safety first—never meet alone in a secluded area. | | **10. Finalize the Sale** | Use a secure payment method (PayPal, Venmo, cash). Sign a simple bill of sale if you want extra protection. | Protects you from fraud and provides a record of the transaction. | ### Quick Tips - **Highlight Unique Features**: If your guitar has a special finish, custom inlay, or upgraded electronics, mention them. - **Be Honest About Wear**: Disclose scratches, dents, or any repairs. Honesty builds buyer confidence. - **Offer a Demo**: If you’re comfortable, let potential buyers try it out. A live demo can close the deal faster. - **Consider Trade‑In**: Some local stores offer trade‑in credits toward a new purchase. ### Example Listing (Reverb) ``` Title: 2015 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition Description: - Brand: Yamaha - Model: FG800 - Year: 2015 - Condition: Like new – no visible wear, strings replaced last month - Features: Solid spruce top, nato/okume back & sides, 20‑string set - Reason for selling: Upgrading to a 12‑string Price: $350 (Negotiable) Photos: [Attach 5–6 high‑resolution images] Shipping: Available via UPS Ground ($15). Local pickup in Seattle available. Payment: PayPal or Venmo. Bill of sale provided upon request. ``` Feel free to adapt this template to your own guitar’s specifics. Good luck with the sale!
